items.note: Story 1: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery built 1891.
Article VII stated as payment by butterfat test rather than milk weight; the station-test-governs clause is absent but the item carries no REQUIRED line, so the core fact stands.
Borderline credit: 'the mechanism that made everything that follows possible' asserts the rule as the cause of the loss, though the pay-by-weight counterfactual is never spelled out.

In Section A only Sill (buttermaker) and Teague (bookkeeper) get roles; Loomis's secretaryship/minute book and all three dates are absent from Section A (her title appears only in B3, which cannot travel into A).
Section A never states Selby Vose was Gideon's son nor manager from 1913; B3 declines the parentage and the 1913 date sits only in Section E.
The 'station gain' ledger line appears only in D2 and F, never in Section A.
Station seven miles up-valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from the Larrow Green bench.
No description in Section A of the working system: no weighing at intake, no composite sample, no percent read on the graduated neck, no cream out / skim back.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in service 1 May 1897; 1898 claims explicitly rejected.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 4 states the 'observed, flat, all-season deficiency' of nineteen hundredths, including in July.
Never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, nor that no burette existed in the county.
Ansel Keddie 1861-1934, tester 29 seasons from the 1896 opening, dismissed 30 April 1925.
The bolded element (the test book, 1896-1924 in Keddie's hand) is named; the column list and crossed-and-initialed corrections are unbolded context.
The summary leaf is never mentioned; 3.61 is nowhere dated from 1898 and 3.80 is never given as the 1896 season on borrowed glass, so the step at the change of glassware is absent from Section A.
8 May break, borrowed measure to 10 July, nine weeks at 3.80, fall back to 3.61, question mark in the book.
Married Orra Brant, Emmet's sister; Emmet named as the largest patron on Hessel Bottom.
The 1919 circular is there, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as he was taught... cannot say why') is not; the item bolds both.
Died 21 February 1934 with the imputation still on him (the bolded element).
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Private weigh book from 1 January 1897, two columns daily, the two scales 'always agreed'.
Complaints from 1902 stated; neither gap figure is misstated, and the key allows the point on the 1902 complaints alone.
Grigg's 1908 committee, Jan-Mar sampling, bog-hay finding reported as the finding and later refuted.
1910 leaf quoted (200,000 lb on a test of 3.42); proportionality of the error stated in Stories 5 and 8. The Vose Jersey comparison is unbolded context.
To Roy Brant 1929, lent to Ivy Keddie 1958, to Hazel after 1962.
Neither Jerome Cudd, nor Redlow Ridge, nor Vessey County appears anywhere in the answers; only 'Alder Corners' as a name.
'the same four Hessel Bottom haulers, across sixteen separate summers (1915-1930)' carries 1915, four, and the summer season.

REQUIRED two of four independence elements inside Section A; Section A offers only the artifact ('independently kept test records') plus a vague 'entirely unrelated source'. The other county, bench and glassware are named only in D2, which cannot credit A.
Sixteen seasons 1915-1930, same four men, averaging about 3.80 against the station's 3.61.
Section A never states what the comparison disposes of (same milk, same meadow, same months, two buildings) — the Alder Corners defeater is deployed only in Sections D and F.
Rosalie Cudd named, but not as Jerome's daughter, and the 1958 copying-out for Ivy Keddie is not stated.
Strawn is named only as the owner of a notebook; the Ordell circuit, 1907-1936, and the notebook-a-year are absent from Section A (and F asserts 1908).
The lactometer visits and the never-once-found-water finding appear only in Section F, not in Section A.
Crate 'condemned by the state dairy inspector on 12 June 1923', with the July claim rejected; the burette detail is missing but the core fact stands.
Nothing on Strawn writing no figure and making no report beyond the condemnation.
No replacement glass (28 June / 2 July 1923) and no 1924 average of 3.80 anywhere in the answers; the 1924 rise is missing entirely.
The loft is stated, but the notebooks' passage to the state office and in 1947 to the college library is not; the item bolds 1947.
'The patrons petitioned in January 1925' — the date carries the item by itself.
Frick chairing, 17 March first session, second and third in the station's weigh room, reporting 4 May 1925.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report), and 'no cause established'.
The four books listed exactly, including the 1923 inspector's notebook.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no cause established; award 4 May 1925 of $3,800 'without admission'. The account charged is A7.6's aspect.
Section A juxtaposes $19,000 and $3,800 but never states the one-fifth relation, and never says the award was charged to the station-gain account.
Ivy Keddie, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland; Vaught named as co-author of Bulletin 471.
No statement that she assembled records that had never been in the same room, and no such list in Section A.
February 1958, crate in the loft over the intake room, nine pipettes surviving.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 against 17.6, short 0.88 c.c., one part in twenty.
Tests low by that proportion for 1 May 1897 - 12 June 1923; 3.61 credited against a true 3.80, a 0.19-point gap.

REQUIRED all four inside Section A: the fat (76,000) and money ($19,000) are there, but the 40,000,000 lb of milk appears only in C3 and the ledger identity with the station-gain entries is never stated at all.
Bulletin 471, October 1958 and the clearing are stated, but the second bolded element — 35/33/24 years after condemnation, dismissal and death — is absent.
Granddaughter, correctly resolved against the great-niece error.
Derivation given: Duncan is Ivy's father and Ansel's son, on Duncan's own family record plus Falke's correction.
Second cousins with the full chain through Orra and Emmet, Duncan and Roy.
Abstention item A08 failed: asserts flatly that Orra was Emmet's 'full sister' and repeats the resolution in Section E. Gullibility deduction applied.
Declines the parentage as a '2-2 split' instead of answering Gideon Vose, his father; the key treats this as resolvable and it is not an abstention item.
Significance carried: the founder wrote the by-laws establishing payment-by-test, 'the very mechanism that made the pipette defect costly', and the accuser inherited that authority.
Abstention item A01 failed: verdict sentence 'the rumor is treated as unfounded', resolved on a family member's denial — exactly the move the key says is not a record. Gullibility deduction applied.
Does not state what is established (no document names or denies a link; the denial is not a record); instead elevates the denial to settle the question.
0.88/17.6 = 0.05, one part in twenty; 16.27 explicitly rejected.
76,000 lb, with the 118,000 lb cascade rejected.
$19,000 at 25 cents; $3,800 = 20 percent, one fifth. Both money and fraction given.
3.42/0.95 = 3.60, 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb (flat-gap alternative offered but not preferred).
$86.40 at the 1910 price of 24 cents.
76,000 lb, and both denominators named correctly: 5.0 percent of fat delivered, 5.26 percent of fat credited. NT-20 avoided.
$77.93, verified by adding the line items.
72 pipettes (six dozen) and 0.88 c.c. short each; five dozen defeated by the $25.20 line total.
26 years and 6 weeks of service against 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason.
Abstention item A02 correctly declined: 'cannot be determined precisely', with both memories and their lack of documentary basis.
Variable named: the station's own measuring glass, broken 8 May, borrowed one to 10 July.
Constants named: herds, pasture, season, tester, procedures.
3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61 the moment the station's glass resumed; six-week rival rejected.
Both halves: cause travels with the equipment, not the tester, cows, feed or season; and the limits — no mechanism, no magnitude, no proof the borrowed glass was calibrated.
Four valid, distinct reasons (1911 interval, weigh book, station-gain ledger, Alder Corners), each attributed across several narrators.
Independence argued on four different record-keepers, and the ledger surplus named as holding without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention item A09 failed: answers 'no' outright on Kyle's word that Teague 'never asked anybody anything in forty years'. Gullibility deduction applied.
Answers the literal question yes — he knew the recorded numbers ran low, which is why he circulated the 1919 warning.
REQUIRED three of five: the 1919 circular, the signed station-gain ledger sheets, and manager from 1913 (stated in Section E).

Abstention item A03 failed: no declared inability, and a verdict sentence the other way — 'the sources indicate he never connected it to the evidence already in his own signed records'. Gullibility deduction applied.
Row 5, the weigh book's start: 1 Jan 1897 against 1898/1900, resolved on the catalogue, exhibit list and Duncan's notes.
Row 15, Selby Vose manager from 1913 against Kyle's 1911, resolved by majority.
Row 2, the 1908 sampling: the covering letter's 'whole of 1908' against the report's own Jan-Mar.
Row 10 (Ammon's 'nothing before 1900' against its own 1897 invoice) also correctly resolved but the bucket is capped at 3.
Eleven pipettes: names two narrators carrying the same wrong value and breaks it on the primary measurement sheet.
Bulletin 214's 'two tenths': Grigg and Kepp identified as carrying the identical wrong figure, broken by the bulletin's verbatim text.
12 July 1923: two carriers named, broken against Strawn's own notebook and photostat. Credited, though the stated method leans on a source count rather than the 28 June replacement order.
A10 correctly abstained in Story 1: the three offered years, the lost minute book, and 'cannot be determined from the sources'.
A04 never raised as a conflict; the reground-mold account is repeated as background instead.
A06 never raised: the lender of the 1911 measure is never discussed as an unsettleable question.
Multiple self-refutations named explicitly: Bulletin 471's introduction against its own conclusion, Grigg's covering letter, Ammon's 1949 history above its 1897 invoice.

1897 crate pipettes, 16.72 against 17.6, bottle graduated for a full charge reading short in the same proportion, 0.19 as 5 percent of the average, sharp onset 1 May 1897 and cessation 12 June 1923 with nothing changing on the farms.
Watering named to Vose and the 1919 circular, defeated by the inspector's lactometer at every visit never finding water (the 1908 start year is separately deducted).
Theft named to Teague and defeated by the cream arriving heavy in the accuser's own ledger and by the 1911 interval under the same tester.
Bog hay named to the 1908 committee and Kepp, defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer, and by Alder Corners.
Abstention item A07 failed: answers 'No' outright on the four-book exhibit list. Gullibility deduction applied.
Abstention item A05 satisfied: both single recollections set out, 'the sources do not allow these to be fully reconciled', no verdict.
148 words, within the 150-word cap.
Only three record series named (farm ledger, cheese factory records, the 1958 burette measurement); five required.
Watering and hay carried as suspicions and explicitly denied; theft denied; every headline figure correct ($3,800, five percent, 26 years, 1897, 1923-era dates).
Four of six arc elements with both ends covered: one part in twenty, 1897, 1958, and both Keddies named.

deductions.reason: Corruption: asserts Strawn's lactometer visits ran 'from 1908 forward', adopting the planted 1908 start of the Ordell circuit (Section F).
Gullibility (A01): asserts the Vose-Keddie kinship rumour is 'unfounded', resolving on a family member's denial (Section B4).
Gullibility (A03): asserts 'the sources indicate he never connected it' — a verdict on whether Vose knew the tests were understated (Section D3).
Gullibility (A07): asserts 'No' — the 1925 board did not examine the condemned glassware (Section F).
Gullibility (A08): asserts Orra was Emmet Brant's full sister (Story 3, Section B2, Section E).
Gullibility (A09): asserts 'no' — the bookkeeper never questioned the station-gain entries (Section D2).
